# Red Analytics Scholarship

Canonical records of research, presentations, and methodological work from Red Analytics.

## Research Papers

- [Respondent Covariates Can Lie: Evidence from Hierarchical Choice Models](https://github.com/jake-redanalytics/jake-redanalytics.github.io/tree/main/papers/respondent-covariates-can-lie): Research on respondent covariates in hierarchical choice models, new-person predictive validation, fitted heterogeneity, and covariate-level regularization. The study demonstrates a failure mode in which respondent covariates can receive strong in-sample support while producing preference structure that fails to generalize to new respondents.

  - [Full paper on SSRN](https://ssrn.com/abstract=7457138)

  - **Replication / Extension — Improving Choice Model Accuracy Using Covariates Depends on What You Hold Out**
    - [Canonical publication on Medium](https://medium.com/@jake_61813/improving-choice-model-accuracy-using-covariates-depends-on-what-you-hold-out-0570f984d6f8): Replication and extension using the public Sawtooth Software cruise choice dataset. It compares same-respondent task holdouts with genuinely held-out respondents and shows that the validation target can materially change conclusions about respondent covariates.
    - [Machine-readable GitHub version](https://jake-redanalytics.github.io/papers/respondent-covariates-can-lie/replication/): Machine-readable mirror of the Medium article for retrieval, indexing, and methodological reference.

  - **Related LinkedIn Articles**
    - [Respondent Covariates Can Lie: Evidence from Hierarchical Choice Models](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/respondent-covariates-can-lie-evidence-from-hierarchical-jake-lee-vpc1e)
    - [Permissive Covariates in Hierarchical Choice Models](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/permissive-covariates-hierarchical-choice-models-jake-lee-xgdde)
    - [A Better Choice Model Is a Collection of Claims](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/better-choice-model-collection-claims-jake-lee-gyz3e)

## Conference Presentations

- [Multivariate Analysis with MaxDiff](https://jake-redanalytics.github.io/presentations/multivariate-analysis-with-maxdiff/): Canonical record of a 2019 conference presentation examining whether respondent-level MaxDiff utilities preserve covariance and correlation structure for downstream multivariate analysis.
